This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any executive summaries task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Validate executive summaries outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
2. State assumptions about executive summaries explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
3. Keep executive summaries changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
4. Before starting executive summaries work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
5. Prefer the simplest executive summaries approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
6. Check that executive summaries terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
7. Measure before optimizing any executive summaries bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
8. Surface known limitations of a chosen executive summaries approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting executive summaries assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid mixing unrelated executive summaries concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop executive summaries edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of executive summaries correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for executive summaries, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
